pr_title: Use saner native measurement units for xiaomi_miio sensors

## Breaking change
<!--

  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you

  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
The sensor values are not reported anymore in the device's native measurement unit (seconds),
but using a more suitable, sensor-specific units:
* Use Time, Total duration, Main Brush Left, Side Brush Left, and Filter Left are now reported in hours
* Last Clean Duration is reported in minutes

<!--

This PR converts the xiaomi_miio vacuum sensor units to more human-readable ones instead of using the device-given, second granularity.

This pull request needs to be manually signed off by @home-assistant/core before it can get merged.
<sub><sup>(message by ReviewEnforcer)</sup></sub>

Hey there @syssi, @starkillerog, @bieniu, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`xiaomi_miio`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L603) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

As the sensors now report seconds, and this PR changes this to a different unit_of_measurement (even different per sensor), would this qualify as a breaking change?

On the other hand: these sensors were new and introduced in 2021.11 and there is a lot pushback on the existing unit_of_measurement, as the previous attributes were already reporting in the unit_of_measurement we're moving to now - so it could also qualify for a bugfix in a 2021.11.x release......

(I'd prefer the last option, because it will fix it before most even see the issue)

> As the sensors now report seconds, and this PR changes this to a different unit_of_measurement (even different per sensor), would this qualify as a breaking change?

Yes, that's why it marked as such (in the PR description at least :-).

> On the other hand: these sensors were new and introduced in 2021.11 and there is a lot pushback on the existing unit_of_measurement, as the previous attributes were already reporting in the unit_of_measurement we're moving to now - so it could also qualify for a bugfix in a 2021.11.x release......

So, looks like I forgot to mark this as a draft, but I don't really know what's the proper solution here so I wanted to just put this up for discussion. I tried to ask on discord if such breaking changes are allowed in point releases with no answer, but I doubt that would be acceptable.

Seconds as native units:
- pro: that's what the device report
- pro: UI / users can chose whichever format they want to have
- con: more data gets pushed into the state machine as every update on a running vacuum is guaranteed to have updated values, although I don't think this is a big issue

"Saner" native units:
- pro: makes it pretty by default in the UI
- con: breaks the rule of not to mix the values to their presentation?

There hasn't been any activity on this pull request recently. This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because of that and will be closed if no further activity occurs within 7 days.
Thank you for your contributions.
Should we go ahead with this? We allow changing the format of time reported to better fit our state machine and use cases, so I think this makes sense.

Agree. It also matches the native app better - seconds aren't really useful here.

![Screenshot_20211205-164007_Mi Home](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33529490/144753293-03484f73-d56c-4ae7-a338-f27a8aa5b228.jpg)

Has anyone besides me tested this already and is there something else that needs to be done at this point? I'm not sure if there are some blockers getting this merged, so if someone could give it a try it'd be great.

edit: To add, I'm personally fine with moving away from second granularity on sensors, so as long there are no objections I'd like to get this merged. As long as there is no sane way to handle the granularity for sensors on the UI (where the conversion should be done, IMO), we should use sane units instead of whatever is provided by the device.
I'll try this out tomorrow and report back :)

issue_context.title: Xiaomi Miio vacuum: change unit_of_measurement for sensors "brush_left", "filter_left", "sensor_dirty_left"
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Starting from 2021.11.0 the following parameters were available from sensors (not from attributes as they were before):
- main brush left;
- side brush left;
- filter left;
- sensor dirty left.

Earlier these parameters were measured in "hours", now the unit is "seconds" which does not make any sense.
Now I have to use template sensors to represent these parameters in hours.

I propose to change unit to "hours".

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.11.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Xiaomi miio

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/xiaomi_miio/#xiaomi-mi-robot-vacuum

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

_No response_

Issue is already raised, and part of architecture discussion. See https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/58923#issuecomment-958392654 (especially 'edit 2').

Let's keep this issue open until this gets a closure. I personally agree that there should be no need for second granularity on any of the sensors in the integration. Besides the fact that the data is polled less often than that, it also causes (imo) unnecessary state machine updates.
I guess the unit for "last_clean_duration" and "total_duration" shouldn't be seconds either.
I am on 2021.12.0b0 and sensors still reporting in seconds.  I was under the impression that would change?  Is this issue being tracked elsewhere?
I'm on 2021.12.7 and same thing. Sensors reporting in seconds

I really hate to whine. It is not my go to, but this change was just stupid. I am sure there was a reason that made sense somewhere.  I just gave up and made template sensors to change all my entities from seconds to hours.
Same. Did that this afternoon until it’s resolved. Back to normal
Same boat guys. The _seconds_ are unusable for me.

You should create separate template sensors to get the wanted values, see the thread starting from https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/59092#discussion_r780354705 - if you are using a some lovelace card to display the data, please report to the card developer that they should use the `native_measurement_unit` and convert the data for display as they see fit.

review_comments:
Besides this being a major breaking change, we should not calculate this inside Home Assistant.

Home Assistant should represent data as is.

So I suppose we should close this?

I agree that this is not the task of the integration while I understand that it's frustrating to users to create separate template sensors or adjust automations (or the UI display) to do the conversions.

> I agree that this is not the task of the integration while I understand that it's frustrating to users to create separate template sensors or adjust automations (or the UI display) to do the conversions.

Yeah, it is a hard balance, as in: We all have preferences, right?

I'd like to recall that this whole discussion started when the upstream package suddenly provided seconds instead of hours for these sensors.

It used to be hours, then it changed to seconds, people not happy, now change (in HA) to go back to hours 🤷🏻
Time is the only thing we allow converting to fit our design. If we want to convert it to lower resolution I think that would be ok.

> Yeah, it is a hard balance, as in: We all have preferences, right?

Right. I think the problem at hand is the fact that while we have native measurement units, we are lacking a way to inform the UI the unit they should be using for displaying the data (or to configure the display unit, for that matter). So maybe all entities should be using the most precise format the device gives, while allowing the integrations to add "unit hints" to signal their preferred display format for UI elements? This discussion doesn't belong to this PR though, so I'll leave it to that and I'll close this PR now.

> I'd like to recall that this whole discussion started when the upstream package suddenly provided seconds instead of hours for these sensors.

That's not true, the upstream package has always delivered seconds. The earlier homeassistant implementation converted the values for display reasons, which was necessary as there was no facilities in homeassistant to report on the used unit (as we have nowadays).
